question.text: If the point $(2 \cos \theta, 2 \sin \theta)$ for $0 \in(0,2 \pi)$ lies in the region between the lines $x+y=2$ and $x-y=2$ containing the origin, then $\theta$ lies in

solution.text: Given that $(2 \cos \theta, 2 \sin \theta)$ will lie on the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ (from the given figure). Since, point lies on the region containing origin. So, point will be on the shaded region. $\therefore$ $\theta \in\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)$
